0.0.n: This is the name of a prefecture in Japan.

0.1.n: Links Osaka Prefecture to its governor; English puts the relationship in the opposite order.

0.2.n: This is the governor’s family name, placed before his title.

0.3.n: This title follows 吉村 without an extra honorific.

0.4.n: Marks Governor Yoshimura as the topic of the sentence.

1.1.n: Short for 万国博覧会, referring here to the World Expo.

1.2.n: Marks the Expo as the topic inside the quotation.

1.4.n: Refers broadly to people around the world.

1.5.n: Marks 世界 as what pays attention to the event.

1.6.n: 注目する uses する with 注目; this phrase describes イベント in the next line.

2.0.n: Borrowed from boxing, this describes the event’s importance and plays on the similar sound of へび, snake.

2.1.n: Connects ヘビー級 to イベント so that the first noun describes the second.

2.2.n: This English loanword is the noun described by both 世界が注目する and ヘビー級の.

2.3.n: Gives the quoted statement a polite ending.

2.5.n: Marks the preceding words as what the governor said.

2.6.n: The て-form of 言う connects this quotation to the following report of his hopes.

3.0.n: Provides the image for the long line of people and echoes the sound of ヘビー級.

3.1.n: Connects へび to よう in the comparison pattern のように.

3.2.n: Works with の and に to express resemblance rather than identify something as an actual snake.

3.3.n: Completes のように, making the snake comparison describe how people line up.

3.4.n: Used with の before 人 to describe a large number of people.

3.5.n: Connects the quantity たくさん to the noun 人.

3.6.n: Japanese nouns do not require a plural ending; たくさん makes the plural sense clear.

3.7.n: Marks たくさんの人 as the people who line up.

4.0.n: 長い changes to 長く to describe how people line up, here emphasizing the line’s length.

4.1.n: The plain form describes the hoped-for queue, not an already completed action.

4.2.n: Sets the desired scale of attendance: enough visitors to form a long queue.

5.0.n: 多く combines with の to describe the number of people.

5.1.n: Connects 多く to 人 to form a phrase describing numerous people.

5.2.n: Refers to the visitors the governor hopes will attend.

5.3.n: Marks the people whom the governor wants to perform the action 来る.

5.4.n: 来る becomes 来て before ほしい; the governor wants other people to come, rather than wanting to come himself.

5.5.n: Marks the preceding wish as the content of what he said.

5.6.n: The polite past form of 話す reports the governor’s statement.

0.lit: As for Osaka Prefecture’s Governor Yoshimura,
0.tip: Japanese puts the prefecture before の and the governor’s title after his name.

1.lit: As for the Expo, the world pays attention to …
1.tip: 世界が注目する describes イベント in the next line: an event the world pays attention to.

2.lit: … a heavyweight event it is, he said, and …
2.tip: と言って closes the quotation and connects it to the rest of the report.

3.tip: のように means like and describes how the people line up in the next line.

4.lit: … to the extent that they line up in a long line,
4.tip: くらい links the imagined long queue to how many visitors he hopes will come.

5.lit: He said he wanted many people to come.
5.tip: 人に来てほしい expresses wanting other people to come, not those people’s own wishes.
